title: Mary, Mother of God (1 January)
hook: the year begins with Mary and, since 1968, the World Day of Peace

segments.voice: Yesterday, tekton: a lost boy in the temple, and then long quiet years at Nazareth. Your line was an ordinary family. Did anyone notice your chore? Day six hundred forty-four.

Midnight on New Year's Eve. Countdowns, fireworks, someone kissing someone, a phone buzzing with messages. Resolutions. Then, a few hours later, while plenty of people are still asleep, the Church holds a solemnity. The first day of the calendar year belongs to a woman: Mary, under her boldest title, Mother of God. And since 1968, it has also been the World Day of Peace. So the year opens twice: once with fireworks, and once with a mother and a prayer for peace.
screen: `MIDNIGHT, JANUARY 1.` → `THE YEAR BELONGS TO A WOMAN.` → `A DAY OF PEACE.`

segments.voice: January 1 is the eighth day after Christmas, the octave day. Luke says that on the eighth day the child was circumcised and named Jesus, and the gospel today returns to the shepherds at the manger. They tell what the angels said, everyone wonders, and then Luke turns to Mary: "But Mary kept all these words, pondering them in her heart." While everyone else talks, she keeps and ponders. The title of the day is a big one. In the year 431, bishops met at Ephesus, in what is now Turkey, to settle an argument. A bishop of Constantinople, Nestorius, had resisted calling Mary Theotokos, God-bearer, preferring Christ-bearer. The council insisted on Theotokos. The argument looks like it's about Mary, but it was really about Jesus: if he is one person, truly God and truly human, then the woman who bore him bore God. Catholic and Orthodox Christians use the title; Protestant churches generally accept the council's teaching about Christ, and some use the title, while speaking about Mary in their own ways. Then in 1968, Pope Paul VI asked that the first day of every year be kept as a day of prayer for peace, and popes since have sent a message for it each year. The first reading is the old priestly blessing from Numbers: "The Lord bless thee, and keep thee." So the year begins with a mother, a blessing and peace. And this week began with seven O's and ended here: o come, a light at midnight, the Word made flesh, the crib and the cross, Rachel weeping, an ordinary family, and now, begin with her.
screen: `THE EIGHTH DAY, AND A NAME.` · `MARY KEPT ALL THESE WORDS.` · `EPHESUS, 431: THEOTOKOS.` · `1968: A DAY FOR PEACE.` · then, large: `THE LORD BLESS THEE, AND KEEP THEE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: a minute for peace, at midnight or right now. Sit, and breathe. Bring to mind one place in the world with no peace tonight, and one place in your own life: a family fight, a cold silence, a grudge. Hold both, the big and the small, without trying to solve them. If you pray, you can ask Mary's help, or say the old blessing over that place, the Lord bless thee and keep thee. If you don't, simply wish peace to both. The bell holds the time.
Mary. The mother of Jesus, honored on January 1 as Mother of God, Theotokos, the one who kept all these words in her heart. Today's word.
Your line: begin with her. Today, before you start something new, stop and ponder for a moment first, the way Mary kept these things in her heart. Day six hundred forty-four.

howItsDone: Catholics keep January 1 as the Solemnity of Mary, the Holy Mother of God, a holy day of obligation in many countries, and the pope issues a message for the World Day of Peace.

fork.setup: you're a bishop at Ephesus in 431. one side wants to call Mary Christ-bearer only. the other, God-bearer. what does the council decide?
fork.reveal: the council affirmed Theotokos. the point was about Jesus: the one she bore is one person, God and man.

original.note: Greek: God-bearer, the title affirmed for Mary at the Council of Ephesus in 431.

trapdoor: what you thought: January 1 is just New Year's Day.
what it means: the octave of Christmas, the Solemnity of Mary, Mother of God, and the World Day of Peace.
what a scholar hears: Ephesus in 431 affirmed Theotokos against Nestorius; the title is a claim about Christ's single person.

notes: Paul VI's message was dated 8 December 1967 for the first World Day of Peace on 1 January 1968. Confirm phrasing.
Description of Protestant views of Theotokos is general; confirm fairness.
Confirm Douay-Rheims wording of Numbers 6:24 and Luke 2:19.
Before 1969, January 1 was kept as the Circumcision of the Lord in the Roman calendar; not mentioned.
Editor review (2026-10-01): cut the garbled 'a whole week looks back at us'; 'many Protestants' softened; practice no longer commands prayer.
